newsitem.title: UK: JET AIRWAYS CHIEF TO BUY OUT 40 PCT STAKE.
newsitem.headline: JET AIRWAYS CHIEF TO BUY OUT 40 PCT STAKE.

text.p: Bombay-based Jet Airways is to buy out the 40 percent share held equally by Gulf Air and Kuwait Airways in the airline's Isle of Man registered company Tail Winds, a Jet spokesman said.

The deal, brought about by tougher government restrictions on foreign stakes in Indian airlines, is expected to be finalised by October 15 and will involve Jet Airways chairman Naresh Goyal, who holds a 60 percent stake in Tail Winds, acquiring the Gulf and Kuwait equity stakes, he told Reuters.
In June, India's Civil Aviation Ministry gave Gulf Air and Kuwait Airways until October 15 to sell their 20 percent stakes in Jet Airways.
The order followed a federal cabinet decision barring foreign airlines from holding equity stakes in the domestic aviation sector.
The spokesman said Goyal has been allowed to operate the airline in India due to his status as a non-resident Indian, living in Britain.
Jet Airways was set up in 1992 and began operations a year later. It has a fleet of 12 Boeing 737s and has recently taken out dry leases on two GECAS B737-400s which are due this month.
It has also placed an order for six B737-800s and four B737-400s with the first to be delivered in October, the official said.

JET, which flies on all the major internal routes in India, has said it is keen to increase its share of the cargo market and has been looking at its own private bonded warehouses to back such expansion.
